title: Ford hopes this Hypercar will be its next Le Mans winner
gist: Ford's still-unnamed LMDh Hypercar—using an ORECA chassis and a 5.4L naturally aspirated V8 derived from the Mustang 'Coyote'—began track testing at Paul Ricard as Ford joins the growing World Endurance Championship Hypercar field alongside McLaren next year, aiming for its first overall Le Mans win since 1969.

themes.theme: Ford's return to top-tier endurance racing

insights.claim: Ford's new LMDh Hypercar began shakedown testing in August using an ORECA carbon-fiber chassis and a 5.4L naturally aspirated V8 derived from the Mustang 'Coyote', joining the Hypercar class alongside McLaren next year.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Motorsport marketing investment; signals continued OEM interest in the growing Hypercar category but limited direct investor relevance.

insights.claim: The surging popularity of the WEC Hypercar category has drawn many manufacturers—Alpine, BMW, Cadillac, Genesis, Porsche, Ferrari, Peugeot, Toyota, Aston Martin—with Ford and McLaren joining next year.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A crowded manufacturer field reflects marketing value OEMs see in endurance racing.
insights.locator: the soaring popularity of the Hypercar category
